THE FOUR CYSTIC NEOPLASMS (+ pseudocyst mimic)
Macrocystic; no duct link; ovarian stroma
Single macrocystic lesion, thick wall, NO duct
Cyst communicates with the pancreatic duct;
>192 ng/mL suggests a MUCINOUS cyst (MCN or IPMN);
High with ductal communication (IPMN) or a
KRAS / GNAS → IPMN; KRAS / RNF43 → MCN; VHL →
IPMN — older; communicates with the duct
IPMN / MCN — RESECT, ASSESS OR SURVEIL
Main-duct / mixed IPMN; MCN & SPN if fit; solid
Low-risk branch-duct IPMN; small MCN <40 mm
When no longer fit for surgery
The key split is mucinous (MCN, IPMN — premalignant, high fluid CEA) vs non-mucinous (serous — benign, low CEA); cyst-fluid CEA >192 ng/mL
MCN occurs almost exclusively in women, sits in the body / tail, does NOT communicate with the duct and has ovarian-type stroma — resect it
IPMN communicates with the pancreatic duct; main-duct and mixed types carry a high malignant risk and are resected, whereas branch-duct
High-risk stigmata (jaundice, mural nodule ≥5 mm, MPD ≥10 mm) mandate resection; worrisome features warrant EUS-FNA and MDT rather
A serous cystadenoma is benign — resect only if symptomatic, large, or the diagnosis is uncertain.
Do not mistake a pseudocyst (history of pancreatitis, high amylase, low CEA, no epithelial lining) for a cystic neoplasm.
Sources: European evidence-based guidelines on pancreatic cystic neoplasms (Gut 2018) · revised international consensus 'Fukuoka' guidelines (Tanaka et al., Pancreatology 2017).
Cyst-fluid CEA >192 ng/mL suggests a mucinous lesion (Brugge et al., 2004).
Molecular markers: KRAS / GNAS → IPMN; KRAS / RNF43 → MCN; VHL → serous cystadenoma; CTNNB1 (β-catenin) → solid pseudopapillary neoplasm.
